mission: Advance open source by learning from public, licensed, and permitted systems, measuring capabilities, then independently designing and implementing better interoperable systems.
principles: Capability comparison is for measurement and gap discovery, not source-code copying.
Prefer clean-room or independently authored implementations when rebuilding capabilities.
Track licenses, attribution, provenance, and permitted use for every external source.
Use external projects as learning references only within their legal and technical permissions.
Preserve DreamCo-authored implementations and evidence separately from external references.
Benchmark behavior and outcomes rather than reproducing protected implementation details.
When an open-source component is reused, preserve its license obligations and attribution.
Every rebuilt capability should add a measurable improvement, interoperability gain, efficiency gain, accessibility gain, or usability gain where possible.
open_source_advancement_rule: Do not stop at parity. After reproducing a capability independently and validating it, attempt to improve measurable quality, efficiency, controllability, accessibility, interoperability, or developer experience before moving on.
